claims.text: The base alloy has the nominal composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Under conventional rapid cooling, the alloy forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases.
The alloy exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence upon reheating.
A short sub-Tg isothermal hold immediately after rapid quenching will suppress primary non-eutectic crystalline-phase formation.
The post-quench sub-Tg hold will enhance amorphous retention.
The post-quench sub-Tg hold will improve thermal stability during subsequent reheating.
Structural relaxation during the sub-Tg hold reduces the number of active heterogeneous nucleation sites.
The reduction in active heterogeneous nucleation sites produces a more homogeneous amorphous structure.
A hold below Tg permits relaxation without driving crystalline nucleation and growth.
The sub-Tg hold minimizes the early formation of crystallite precursors.
Minimizing crystallite precursors delays crystallization during subsequent reheating.
Compared with rapid quenching alone, the treated alloy will retain a higher amorphous fraction at room temperature.
Compared with rapid quenching alone, the treated alloy will show a delayed crystallization exotherm during thermal analysis.
Compared with rapid quenching alone, the treated alloy will show reduced crystallization-exotherm intensity or area.
Cooling above a critical rate can bypass significant equilibrium crystallization in this alloy.
A narrow temperature window below Tg avoids nucleation while permitting structural relaxation.
The treatment is expected to increase the Tg-Tx interval relative to rapid quenching alone.

contradictions.description: The baseline says rapid quenching produces extensive primary crystallization, whereas the conditions assume rapid cooling above a critical threshold that bypasses significant crystallization; no distinct cooling rates or numerical boundary reconcile these statements.

The hold occurs only after quenching, so it cannot suppress primary crystals that already formed during prior solidification. The stated mechanism addresses precursor evolution and crystallization on reheating rather than removal or prevention of pre-existing primary phases.

The intervention is explicitly below Tg, but the mechanism describes the material during the hold as a supercooled liquid; below Tg it would ordinarily be treated as an amorphous solid undergoing structural relaxation.
